entry.title: A last turn before a toy goes
entry.summary: When you are passing an outgrown toy to another child or family, Davies suggests helping your toddler understand where it is going and offering one last turn.
entry.cue: An outgrown toy is leaving the home, and your child still wants a turn with it.
detail: She separates storing a toy for later rotation from letting an outgrown one leave the home. For something being passed on, the child can have a final play, put it in the box when finished, and help carry the box out.

If the box cannot leave straight away, she puts it out of view so the child does not have to go through the parting again. This is a way to involve them in a real change, not a demand that they stop caring about the toy.
